This week, SAHARI teams continued their dedicated support to local farmers through ongoing agricultural extension services, ensuring that farmers receive the guidance they need during this critical stage of the season. Meanwhile, project monitoring activities are actively taking place across all sites to track progress and address emerging challenges. The team is also documenting two inspiring success stories that reflect the positive change the project is bringing to rural communities.

4th Jan to 8th Jan
2. BRDO 
Weekly Update 
BRDO continued follow-up with newly formed small producer associations, providing training and technical assistance on saving practices, resource mobilization, and asset utilization (e.g., using equipment as collateral). 
•	Coverage: 5 male associations (150 members) and 1 women’s association (40 members). 
Key Issues 
Under Sudanese law, small producers must be organized in registered associations to access loans. However, even registered groups face significant barriers, as banks and private sector actors are often reluctant to provide financing. Associations also have limited advocacy and negotiation capacity, and there are no formal platforms that bring together associations, banks, and the private sector to address constraints and explore joint solutions. 
1. Practical Action 
This week focused on follow-up of micro-grant activities in Halfa locality, particularly group-based income-generating projects. 
•	Sewing groups: Women’s groups trained on garment production have begun operating within their neighborhoods. A field visit was conducted in Koubri 5 Village, covering 20 women (ages 18–35). 
•	Food processing: Beneficiaries of peanut butter (dukwa) machines have started production, with products already entering local markets. Marketing opportunities are promising in Halfa market and nearby neighborhoods, especially ahead of Ramadan. Plans are also underway to introduce chickpea grinding due to high seasonal demand. 
•	Grain mills: A monitoring visit was conducted in Jaber Village, covering 20 women (ages 18–35). 
Challenges 
Despite positive progress, beneficiary groups face limited market access and strong dependence on seasonal demand. Weak marketing capacity and market linkages may affect the sustainability and scalability of these women-led initiatives unless addressed through targeted technical and business development support.

 Practical Action Organization
•	In coordination with the Agricultural Extension Departments in Halfa and Wad Al-Hileu field visits were organized to monitor lentil harvesting currently on-going.
•	Community Management Committees (CMCs) were engaged in project closure meetings in each community, with joint development of post-project sustainability plans, particularly for Micro-Grant activities. These include community-led monitoring, reporting, and accountability systems. 
•	Follow-up mechanisms were established for 135 previously distributed goats (35 male, 100 female), focusing on animal health, reproduction, and productivity. A pass-on scheme will extend benefits to 100 additional households. 
•	Veterinary support is being provided through 20 trained CAHWs (15 in Halfa, 5 in Wad Al-Hileu), delivering basic services, disease surveillance, vaccinations, and awareness on livestock management.
